content: The mosquito coil testing process involves the following steps: 1. Selection of Coils: Randomly select 20 boxes of mosquito coils. From each box, pick one single coil. Discard any coils that are broken or cracked due to improper handling during the separation process. 2. Breaking Load Test: Each of the 20 selected coils is subjected to a breaking load test. A single mosquito coil is placed within a plastic device that supports it using opposite grooves. On one side, the groove supports only 2 cm of the coil from its tip. The coil and the plastic device are then placed on a flat platform of a 500 g scale. 3. Application of Load: A pointed screw is lowered and adjusted to fit into the head or eye of the coil. The screw is gently and gradually turned clockwise, applying pressure to the coil until it breaks. The breaking point is recorded on the scale. 4. Minimum Specification: The standard minimum breaking load for a mosquito coil is 120 g. The procedure is repeated for the remaining 19 coils. 5. Separation of Twin Coils: To separate twin mosquito coils: Break the connecting points at the ends of the coils. Hold both heads or eyes of the double coils with thumbs and forefingers. Gently push the heads or eyes in opposite directions and pull them apart to separate them into single coils. Gentle twisting may be applied if necessary. A satisfactory separation is achieved if no breakage occurs. 6. Storage and Stability Testing: Samples of the formulation should be analyzed both before and after the storage stability test to minimize analytical errors. Samples must be stored in conditions that prevent material deterioration, and sampling instruments must be clean and dry to avoid contamination. 7. Packaging Requirements: Each unit container should contain at least one mosquito coil stand or holder, which must be made of suitable non-flammable materials capable of holding the burning coil stably. For vaporizing mats (MV): 1. Material Composition: The vaporizing mat should consist of a pulp-made or inert material impregnated with an insecticide. Stabilizers, synergists, slow-release agents, perfumes, and coloring agents may be added. The mat is designed for use in a heating unit that facilitates slow volatilization of the active ingredient. 2. Identity Tests: The active ingredient must comply with an identity test. If the identity remains uncertain, it must pass at least one additional test. The declared content of the active ingredient (mg/mat) must not deviate by more than ±15% from the measured average content. 3. Mat Size: The mat size must be compatible with the associated heater to ensure proper functionality. 4. Sampling and Testing: Samples must be drawn from each lot and tested individually to ensure compliance with specified requirements. Any defective sample is deemed unacceptable. The acceptance number is the maximum permissible number of defective samples for a lot to be accepted. For liquid vaporizers (LV): 1. Product Description: The liquid vaporizer consists of a liquid insecticide formulation in a cartridge or bottle designed to fit a suitable heater unit. The formulation must effectively evaporate at a suitable rate over the claimed period. The cartridge or bottle must minimize the risk of accidental ingestion and include a child-proof cap. 2. Wick Requirements: The wick must be made of a porous, heat-resistant material capable of drawing up sufficient insecticide for vaporization. It should be designed to vaporize the entire content of the insecticide formulation in the attached bottle or cartridge. 3. Minimum Effective Period: The minimum effective period must be declared, and the cartridge or bottle must contain enough formulation to function for at least the declared period. 4. Sampling and Testing: Samples must be drawn from each lot and tested individually. Defective samples are not acceptable, and the acceptance number determines the maximum permissible defective samples for a lot to be accepted. For aerosol dispensers (AE): 1. Product Description: The aerosol dispenser contains a liquid formulation in a pressurized, non-refillable container with propellants, synergists, and other formulants. It is designed to release the active ingredient into the air as an aerosol. 2. Active Ingredient Tests: The active ingredient must comply with an identity test and, if necessary, at least one additional test. 3. Net Content: The minimum net content must be declared, and the average net content must not be lower than the declared value. 4. Valve Functionality: The aerosol dispenser valves must not clog during testing. The combined weight of the container and contents must not fall below a specified percentage of the original weight. 5. Corrosion Resistance: Aerosol dispensers are expected to resist corrosion for at least two years from the date of release by the manufacturer. However, no practical method currently exists to predict structural integrity beyond this period. 6. Sampling and Testing: Samples must be drawn from each lot and tested individually. Defective samples are not acceptable, and the acceptance number determines the maximum permissible defective samples for a lot to be accepted. These procedures ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of mosquito coils, vaporizing mats, liquid vaporizers, and aerosol dispensers.
